thread.title: Apple ( AAPL ) has been one of the darlings on this run high

author: Taylor Dart
title: Apple ( AAPL ) has been one of the darlings on this run high
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) has been one of the darlings on this run higher, and one of the first names I went long after the market broke to new highs. The stock had a tremendous 70% run all while trending above its 40-week moving average, but this all came to a screeching halt last week. Given this new development and change of character in the stock, I have exited my position for a gain of over $50.00 per share from my $104.40 entry in Q3 of 2016. This does not mean that Apple is broken and must go lower from here, but based on my time-frame and strategy, this is a red light signal that tells me to exit my position. The fact that the stock was out-performing and leading the indexes over the past year and a half was a great sign, but this has now changed and the stock is a laggard based on recent weakness.
In August of 2016, Apple had spent nearly a year below its 40-week moving average and finally reclaimed it. This gave me a new signal to go long the stock at the beginning of the week following the 40-week moving average reclamation at $104.40. Often this signal alerts me to a change of character in a stock as it moves from laggard to leader, and in this case the signal turned out to be a profitable one.
(Source: TC2000.com)
Taking a look at the below weekly chart of Apple, we can see that the stock briefly back-tested its 40-week moving average after this signal, but then went on a massive run afterward. I sold 1/4 of my position on the way up at $154.20 to lock in nearly a 50% gain, but continued to trail my stop per my strategy at a close below the 40-week moving average. After the nasty week ending on February 2nd I cut another 1/4 of my position at $159.18, and cut the remainder of the position on Friday at $156.20. This gave me an average selling price of $156.45, and a $52.00 gain on the position.
